# BLE Setup — GATT Database Patterns

This skill generates GATT database files directly. The Bluetooth Configurator (`design.cybt` → `GeneratedSource/`) is NOT required — the output format is deterministic and AI-generatable.

> **When to mention the Configurator:** If the user has an existing `design.cybt` file or asks about the Configurator specifically, note that it's an alternative visual tool available in the ModusToolbox IDE. The files generated below are functionally identical to Configurator output.

---

## File Structure

Two files are generated in the project root (or NS sub-project root for PSE84):

| File | Contains |
|---|---|
| `app_bt_gatt_db.h` | Handle `#define`s, extern declarations, device name macro |
| `app_bt_gatt_db.c` | Binary GATT database array, length variable |

---

## Handle Numbering Convention

Handles are 16-bit values. Use a consistent offset scheme per service:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HDLS_` | Service declaration handle |
| `HDLC_` | Characteristic declaration handle |
| `HDLC_*_VALUE` | Characteristic value handle (where data lives) |
| `HDLD_` | Descriptor handle (CCCD, format, user description) |

Start custom services at handle `0x0028` (after mandatory GAP/GATT services which occupy `0x0001`–`0x0027`).

Each service block increments by `0x0010` to leave room for future characteristics:
- Service 1: `0x0028` – `0x0037`
- Service 2: `0x0038` – `0x0047`
- etc.

---

## Template: app_bt_gatt_db.h

```c
/*******************************************************************************
 * File: app_bt_gatt_db.h
 *
 * Description: GATT database handle definitions.
 * Generated by AI assistant — equivalent to Bluetooth Configurator output.
 ******************************************************************************/

#ifndef APP_BT_GATT_DB_H
#define APP_BT_GATT_DB_H

#include "wiced_bt_types.h"

#define APP_BT_DEVICE_NAME          "MY-DEVICE-NAME"
#define APP_BT_DEVICE_NAME_LEN      (sizeof(APP_BT_DEVICE_NAME) - 1)

/* Service: Generic Access (mandatory) */
#define HDLS_GAP                            0x0001
#define HDLC_GAP_DEVICE_NAME                0x0002
#define HDLC_GAP_DEVICE_NAME_VALUE          0x0003
#define HDLC_GAP_APPEARANCE                 0x0004
#define HDLC_GAP_APPEARANCE_VALUE           0x0005

/* Service: Generic Attribute (mandatory) */
#define HDLS_GATT                           0x0006

/* --- Custom Services Start Here --- */

/* Service: Custom Service (example) */
#define HDLS_CUSTOM_SERVICE                 0x0028
#define HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW                 0x0029
#define HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW_VALUE           0x002A
#define HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY             0x002B
#define HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY_VALUE       0x002C
#define HDLD_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY_CCCD        0x002D

/* Extern declarations */
extern const uint8_t gatt_database[];
extern const uint16_t gatt_database_len;

#endif /* APP_BT_GATT_DB_H */
```

---

## Template: app_bt_gatt_db.c

The GATT database is a packed binary array following the Bluetooth ATT protocol format. Each entry is:
`[length_byte, handle_hi, handle_lo, UUID..., permissions, value...]`

```c
/*******************************************************************************
 * File: app_bt_gatt_db.c
 *
 * Description: GATT database definition.
 * Generated by AI assistant — equivalent to Bluetooth Configurator output.
 ******************************************************************************/

#include "app_bt_gatt_db.h"
#include "wiced_bt_uuid.h"
#include "wiced_bt_gatt.h"

/*******************************************************************************
 * GATT Database
 ******************************************************************************/
const uint8_t gatt_database[] = {

    /* ===== Primary Service: Generic Access (0x1800) ===== */
    /* Service declaration */
    PRIMARY_SERVICE_UUID16(HDLS_GAP, UUID_SERVICE_GAP),

    /* Device Name characteristic — read-only */
    CHARACTERISTIC_UUID16(HDLC_GAP_DEVICE_NAME, HDLC_GAP_DEVICE_NAME_VALUE,
        UUID_CHARACTERISTIC_DEVICE_NAME,
        GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_READ,
        GATTDB_PERM_READABLE),

    /* Appearance characteristic — read-only */
    CHARACTERISTIC_UUID16(HDLC_GAP_APPEARANCE, HDLC_GAP_APPEARANCE_VALUE,
        UUID_CHARACTERISTIC_APPEARANCE,
        GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_READ,
        GATTDB_PERM_READABLE),

    /* ===== Primary Service: Generic Attribute (0x1801) ===== */
    PRIMARY_SERVICE_UUID16(HDLS_GATT, UUID_SERVICE_GATT),

    /* ===== Primary Service: Custom Service ===== */
    PRIMARY_SERVICE_UUID128(HDLS_CUSTOM_SERVICE, UUID_CUSTOM_SERVICE),

    /* Read/Write characteristic */
    CHARACTERISTIC_UUID128_WRITABLE(HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW, HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW_VALUE,
        UUID_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW,
        GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_READ | GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_WRITE,
        GATTDB_PERM_READABLE | GATTDB_PERM_WRITE_REQ),

    /* Notify characteristic */
    CHARACTERISTIC_UUID128(HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY, HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY_VALUE,
        UUID_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY,
        GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_READ | GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_NOTIFY,
        GATTDB_PERM_READABLE),

    /* Client Configuration Descriptor (CCCD) for notifications */
    CHAR_DESCRIPTOR_UUID16_WRITABLE(HDLD_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY_CCCD,
        UUID_DESCRIPTOR_CLIENT_CHARACTERISTIC_CONFIGURATION,
        GATTDB_PERM_READABLE | GATTDB_PERM_WRITE_REQ),
};

const uint16_t gatt_database_len = sizeof(gatt_database);
```

---

## Custom 128-bit UUID Definition

Define UUIDs for custom services/characteristics. Generate random UUIDs or use application-specific ones:

```c
/* In app_bt_gatt_db.c — above the gatt_database array */

/* Custom Service UUID: 12345678-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB (example)
 * Stored in LITTLE-ENDIAN byte order for BTSTACK */
#define UUID_CUSTOM_SERVICE \
    0xFB, 0x34, 0x9B, 0x5F, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80, \
    0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12

#define UUID_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW \
    0xFB, 0x34, 0x9B, 0x5F, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80, \
    0x00, 0x10, 0x01, 0x00, 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12

#define UUID_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY \
    0xFB, 0x34, 0x9B, 0x5F, 0x80, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80, \
    0x00, 0x10, 0x02, 0x00, 0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12
```

> **UUID generation:** For truly custom services, generate a random UUID v4. Modify bytes 12-15 of the base UUID for each characteristic within the same service.

---

## Standard Bluetooth SIG Profiles

For standard profiles, use the assigned 16-bit UUIDs:

| Profile | Service UUID | Common Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| Heart Rate | `0x180D` | Heart Rate Measurement (0x2A37, Notify), Body Sensor Location (0x2A38, Read) |
| Battery | `0x180F` | Battery Level (0x2A19, Read + Notify) |
| Environmental Sensing | `0x181A` | Temperature (0x2A6E), Humidity (0x2A6F) |
| Device Information | `0x180A` | Manufacturer Name (0x2A29), Model Number (0x2A24), FW Revision (0x2A26) |

Example using 16-bit service UUID:

```c
PRIMARY_SERVICE_UUID16(HDLS_HEART_RATE, 0x180D),

CHARACTERISTIC_UUID16(HDLC_HR_MEASUREMENT, HDLC_HR_MEASUREMENT_VALUE,
    0x2A37,
    GATTDB_CHAR_PROP_NOTIFY,
    GATTDB_PERM_NONE),

CHAR_DESCRIPTOR_UUID16_WRITABLE(HDLD_HR_MEASUREMENT_CCCD,
    UUID_DESCRIPTOR_CLIENT_CHARACTERISTIC_CONFIGURATION,
    GATTDB_PERM_READABLE | GATTDB_PERM_WRITE_REQ),
```

## Sending Notifications

After the client writes `0x0001` to the CCCD, send notifications with:

```c
/* Application data buffer */
static uint8_t notify_data[20];  /* Adjust size to characteristic value length */

void app_send_notification(uint16_t conn_id, uint16_t attr_handle,
                           uint8_t *data, uint16_t len)
{
    wiced_bt_gatt_server_send_notification(conn_id, attr_handle, len, data, NULL);
}
```

> **Track CCCD state:** Maintain a variable (e.g., `static uint8_t cccd_flags`) that records whether the client has enabled notifications. Only call `send_notification` when `cccd_flags != 0`. Update this variable in the GATT write handler when `HDLD_*_CCCD` handles are written.

---

## GATT Attribute Lookup Table Pattern

For the read/write handlers, maintain a lookup table mapping handles to application data:

```c
typedef struct {
    uint16_t handle;
    uint16_t max_len;
    uint16_t cur_len;
    uint8_t  *p_data;
} gatt_db_lookup_table_t;

/* Application state variables */
static uint8_t app_custom_rw_value[20] = {0};
static uint8_t app_custom_notify_cccd[2] = {0};

static gatt_db_lookup_table_t app_gatt_db_ext[] = {
    { HDLC_CUSTOM_CHAR_RW_VALUE,       20, 0, app_custom_rw_value },
    { HDLD_CUSTOM_CHAR_NOTIFY_CCCD,    2,  2, app_custom_notify_cccd },
    /* Add entries for each readable/writable handle */
};

/* Lookup function */
gatt_db_lookup_table_t *app_get_attribute(uint16_t handle)
{
    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(app_gatt_db_ext)/sizeof(app_gatt_db_ext[0]); i++)
    {
        if (app_gatt_db_ext[i].handle == handle)
            return &app_gatt_db_ext[i];
    }
    return NULL;
}
```

This pattern is used by all PSE84 BLE code examples and provides clean separation between GATT protocol handling and application logic.
